subject: Order in melt()-formula: Why not respected?

messages.author: 20a857807016d58a
messages.subject: Order in melt()-formula: Why not respected?
parts:
Dear all,

why is the order of the columns given by the formula in melt not
respected?

library(reshape2)
ar <- array(1:24, dim=c(2,3,4), dimnames=list(dim1=c("11","12"),
dim2=c("21","22","23"),
dim3=c("31","32","33","34")))
melt(ar, formula = . ~ dim2 + dim1 + dim3) # dim1, dim2, then dim3
instead of dim2, dim1, then dim3

Cheers,

Marius

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Order in melt()-formula: Why not respected?
parts:
Hi:

Try this instead:

melt(aperm(ar, c(2, 1, 3)))
dim2 dim1 dim3 value
1 21 11 31 1
2 22 11 31 3
3 23 11 31 5
4 21 12 31 2
5 22 12 31 4
6 23 12 31 6
...

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Order in melt()-formula: Why not respected?
parts:
Actually, it's more than that. melt() returns a data frame, not an
array, so you could just as easily have permuted the columns of the
data frame to get them the way you want:

> melt(ar)[c(2, 1, 3, 4)]

but the sort order in this case is (1 -> 2 -> 3) rather than (2 -> 3
-> 1); that's what aperm() gets you.

HTH,
Dennis
